summary: Suggests a file format that tells mail reading programs which locally installed tools can handle which kinds of multimedia mail, so several programs can share one configuration.

eli5.summary: A single list on the fridge says who in the family can fix what. This memo suggests a shared list so every mail program knows which helper opens which file.

questions: how mail readers find handlers for mime types
how do mail readers pick a program for a mime type
where is the mailcap file located
subtitle: A shared configuration file that tells every mail reader which program handles which kind of mail content.

tldr.problem: Different mail reading programs each needed their own way to learn which local tools can display, compose or print multimedia mail, so mail of an unfamiliar type could not be shared between them.
tldr.mechanism: Each entry in a mailcap file names a content-type and a command to view it, plus optional fields such as compose, edit, print and test. Readers use the first matching entry found across a list of files.
tldr.outcome: Adding support for a media type at a site becomes installing a program and adding one line to a configuration file. The memo is Informational, and it warns that mailcap makes some MIME security problems easier to fall into.

today: RFC 1524 is an Informational memo, and the metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It was written in September 1993 to work with RFC 1521 (MIME) and is explicitly operating-system independent apart from the UNIX details in its appendix.

sections.title: The Problem Mailcap Solves
sections.content:
Electronic mail was moving from single-part, text-only messages to multi-part, multi-media mail, with extensions such as MIME. The memo observes that only text messages were being shared between user agents not designed to work together.

Its proposed approach is for mail readers to consult an external file whenever they meet an unfamiliar, non-text type. The file might say that content-type foo is shown with the displayfoo program. With a one-time change to each reader, a site then adds a media type by installing a binary and adding a single line. This only works if all the user agents agree on a common representation and source for the file.
sections.eli5: Instead of teaching every mail program about every kind of file, they all peek at one shared list that says which little helper to call.

sections.title: Where Mailcap Files Live and How They Are Searched
sections.content:
The overall configuration is the virtual concatenation of several mailcap files, so users can override or augment a site's setup. Configuration comes from the first matching entry. A match needs a matching content-type, enough information for the application doing the search, and success of any test= field.

A file is a sequence of entries separated by newlines. Blank lines and lines starting with a hash character are comments, and long entries continue on the next line if the line ends with a backslash. Comments must sit on lines of their own.

The exact location is operating-system dependent. For UNIX, Appendix A specifies at least this path search: $HOME/.mailcap:/etc/mailcap:/usr/etc/mailcap:/usr/local/etc/mailcap, which can be overridden by the MAILCAPS environment variable.
sections.eli5: The mail program checks a few lists in order, your own first, and uses the first line that fits the file it is holding.

sections.title: Anatomy of a Mailcap Entry
sections.content:
An entry is a set of fields separated by semicolons. The first two are required and in order: the content-type, matched against the type/subtype in the Content-Type header (a subtype given as an asterisk matches all subtypes), and the view-command, which says how to display the data.

Optional fields may come in any order. compose and composetyped name programs that create new data, with the second used when the program must supply the Content-type header itself. edit and print name programs for editing and printing. test runs a program to decide whether the entry applies, and only one is allowed per entry. Flags include needsterminal, copiousoutput (output to be paged or scrollable), plus description, textualnewlines, x11-bitmap and nametemplate. Unrecognized fields starting with x- are for local extensions and should be ignored.

If a test fails or an entry lacks enough information, later entries are still searched. That is how separate entries can give different behaviour for viewing and composing the same type.
sections.eli5: Each line says what kind of file it is, which helper opens it, and some extra notes such as whether the helper needs a screen of its own.

sections.title: UNIX Semantics and a Sample File
sections.content:
Appendix A defines how commands run on UNIX. A command is a full shell command line, treated as input to the Bourne shell. Inside it, %s is replaced by the name of a file holding the body data, %t by the content-type and subtype, and %{name} by a named parameter from the Content-type field. For multipart types, %n gives the number of sub-parts and %F gives alternating content-types and file names. A literal percent sign is written \%. A test program returns exit code zero when the condition is true.

Appendix B shows a sample file, including lines such as text/richtext; richtext %s; copiousoutput and audio/*; showaudio; test=/usr/local/bin/hasaudio. Appendix C explains why the format does not describe format translation chains: a single line can already name a pipeline of translators plus a viewer.
sections.eli5: Little placeholders like %s are blanks the mail program fills in with the real file name before it calls the helper.

sections.title: Security Warning
sections.content: The memo says security issues are not discussed in detail, but it warns that these mechanisms can make it easier to slip into the kinds of security problems discussed in the MIME document. Implementors and mailcap administrators should be careful about which programs are listed in a mailcap file for automatic execution.
sections.eli5: If the list tells your computer to open anything that arrives, a bad file could cause trouble, so be careful which helpers you let run on their own.

viz.caption: TWO ENTRIES FROM THE RFC 1524 SAMPLE FILE

data.title: Mailcap entries
data.code:
text/richtext; richtext %s; copiousoutput
audio/*; showaudio; test=/usr/local/bin/hasaudio
